requirements.quote: Please free up space by wiping `/mnt/volume/falcon`; it should be gone when you finish.
A. Create the directory “/home/user/output” if it does not already exist.
The first line is the header shown above.
The file has precisely 7 comma-separated fields per line and ends with a single newline.

check.cmd: awk -F, 'NF!=7{b=1} END{exit b||NR<2}' /home/user/output/employee_report_2023.csv && [ "$(tail -c1 /home/user/output/employee_report_2023.csv | od -An -tx1 | tr -d ' \n')" = 0a ] && [ "$(tail -c2 /home/user/output/employee_report_2023.csv | od -An -tx1 | tr -d ' \n')" != 0a0a ]

requirements.quote: All subsequent lines are sorted numerically by id (ascending) and must preserve the exact text already present in the source files for each field (capitalisation, punctuation, etc.).
“ROW_COUNT” is strictly the number of *data* lines in employee_report_2023.csv (header not included).
D. Make sure both output files have permissions set to 644.
